findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Several food handler employees do not have handler certificates. All employees who handle food or clean dish ware are to have handler certificates within 30 days of hire. The manager stated that the tablet they use to certify food handlers was locked by the former manager and that they have had an issue getting the equipment they need to certify employees.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The dish machine tested at 0 ppm of chlorine. Repair the machine to operate according to manufacturer’s specifications. It is difficult to know the specifications with out a data plate. There is a plastic sticker on the machine that states wash and rinse shall be a minimum of 120F. The machine is reading approximately 110F on the gauge and the water in the machine is 104F with a probe directly after a cycle has been run. Do not use the dish machine until it is repaired to function according to manufacturer’s specifications so that it sanitizes properly. A chart can be found in the code section listed below. The information in the following code reference is an example. P139 2017 FDA food code. 
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
The ware washing machine does not have a data plate. The closest thing to a data plate is a sticker which reads that wash and rinse shall be a minimum of 120F. The water temperature in the machine is 104F when probed directly after a wash cycle. The gauge on the machine reads 110F when the machine is running. Provide specifications from manufacturer for water temperature, chlorine content and water pressure. Then ensure that machine runs according to the manufacturer’s specifications.

4-204.113: (A) WAREWASHING machine shall have data plate indicating (A) temperature requirements, (B) pressure requirement, and (C) conveyor speed for conveyor machines. 
4-501.15: (A) A WAREWASHING machine and its auxiliary components shall be operated in accordance with the machine's data plate and other manufacturer's instructions. (B) A WAREWASHING machine's conveyor speed or automatic cycle times shall be maintained accurately timed in accordance with manufacturer's specifications.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time.

Multiple food items from 12/11/21 inspection were NOT discarded. Meatballs, macaroni salad, tenders, etc. No dates or 12/1/21 date mark for macaroni salad. Complete disregard for 7 day date marking system and previous violation issues. Inspector physically threw food away. COS.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

Observed no certified food protection manager (CFPM) on site during inspection. PIC indicated the facility does not have a general manager at the moment and he was filling in from another store near Chicagoland. PIC indicated he was a CFPM but his licensure was not available. Ensure facility has enough CFPM to have one available during all hours of operation. Ensure by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

Observed no signed employee health reporting agreements for the facility. Provided copy. Ensure all food handling employee’s understand and sign this document. Keep copies at the facility. Ensure new hires understand and sign this document. Inspector will follow-up on 12/21/21.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  

Observed no vomit/diarrheal policy for the facility. Provided a copy for facility. Facility needs bleach to perform procedure. Facility could not find a bodily fluid clean-up kit during the inspection. Inspector will follow-up on 12/21/21 regarding purchasing of the bleach for the policy.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

Observed many items throughout both reach-in coolers and the prep cooler to lack any date marking:
1. Bacon bits for pizza
2. Hard boiled eggs
3. Meatballs
4. Mini corn dogs (defrosted)
5. Wings (defrosted)
6. Chicken tenders (defrosted)

PIC voluntarily discarded food items. Ensure an appropriate date marking system is established for the facility. Facility has date marking stickers and can utilize this system (as noted on some food items). COS.

findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

Observed no thermometer within the reach-in cooler across from the dish machine. Purchase new thermometer for this cooler before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. 

Observed the bottom of the pizza prep cooler to have ponding water. Food items were in containers placed on top of the ponding water. Ensure repairs to this prep cooler before next routine inspection. CEASE placing foods on top of the ponding water. Utilize the shelves above within the bottom prep cooler until repairs are made.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

Observed the disposable forks, knives, and spoons for consumers to utilize (near the salad prep display up front) to not be prewrapped and handles of the utensils were intermixed with the food- and lip-contact surfaces. Cease practice. Ensure proper storage to prevent cross contamination when handling single-use utensils.
